articles.title: Paramount and State A.G. to Meet Monday to Discuss Settlement of Antitrust Case
articles.summary: Paramount Skydance representatives are expected to meet on Monday with the California Attorney General’s office to discuss a potential settlement of the states’ antitrust case, according to two sources familiar with the situation.
body: Bonta led a 12-state coalition to challenge the merger in July, arguing that it would illegally contract the marketplace for theatrical distribution and basic cable. The merger would consolidate two of Hollywood’s five legacy studios and two of the top three cable programmers.

Under federal rules, the two sides will have to at least try to settle the case in front of a magistrate judge at some point. At a hearing this week, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin asked the parties to identify two potential magistrates who could oversee mediation by next Wednesday.

A parade of interested parties has recently come out in favor of a settlement, including the Directors Guild of America, IATSE, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and Cinema United, the trade group representing theater chains.

“Earlier this week, you heard the attorney general himself say he’d prefer this settle in the boardroom, not the courtroom,” Gov. Gavin Newsom said Friday. “I think there’s some universal sentiment there, if that’s possible. The question is is that possible. And what’s the best deal? That has to be worked through. That’s a process that’s unfolding, I assure you, in real time.”

articles.title: Emmy Overachiever Jason Bateman on Whether He Considers Himself an Actor or Director First
articles.summary: Jason Bateman is this year’s Emmy overachiever, nominated for lead limited series actor and limited series directing on Netflix’s “Black Rabbit,” and as both supporting actor and executive producer on another limited series, HBO Max’s “DTF St.
body: Awards Circuit Podcast: The 'Black Rabbit' star/director and 'DTF St. Louis' star/producer on his multiple nominations and more. On the Awards Circuit Roundtable, we look at the state of the race as Phase 2 voting continues.

“I’m enormously grateful that I’m still working in this industry in this town,” he says. “I mean, I’ve gained a lot of experience in this business, and one of the things that’s really clear to me is that the best people are not guaranteed employment.”

Bateman, of course, saw that firsthand in the lean years that came prior to “Arrested Development,” which set his career on a new, lucrative course that eventually included smashes like Netflix’s “Ozark,” his podcast “SmartLess” with buddies Will Arnett and Sean Hayes, and then most recently the back-to-back success of “Black Rabbit” and “DTF St. Louis.” Bateman talked about all that, as well as his next project — and he took the Awards Circuit Podcast 10 Questions Quiz! — on this edition.

articles.title: Secret Hollywood Group’s AI Plan Focuses on Defining How AI Is Used — While Keeping Humans in Control
articles.summary: A group of Hollywood filmmakers, executives and actors has spent the last three years secretly meeting with Silicon Valley executives to try to address a simmering issue in the industry: how to define where AI is useful in the context of a human-controlled creative process.
body: The convening of Hollywood leaders to reshape the conversation around AI comes as the industry grapples with how the transformational technology can be additive to the filmmaking process while recognizing the fear that generative AI has struck into the creative community over everything from how models are trained to the rise of AI-generated deepfakes. The initiative indicates that industry execs and creative professionals are more eager to publicly discuss AI’s place within Hollywood, even if attendees are selectively going public about it.

The “ Human Generative Workflows ” document is intended to “stimulate industry discussion and provide a common vocabulary for thinking about authorship in an era of generative AI,” the group said in its first public statement. The group acknowledged that the document wasn’t intended to address some of the more pressing issues surrounding AI, such as how models are trained and the potential impact on jobs.

articles.title: David Harbour has blown Tony Stark’s cover in Avengers: Doomsday. It might just be what Marvel needs
articles.summary: The actor, who plays Red Guardian in the film, made a cryptic comment to Variety that raised more Robert Downey Jr-shaped questions than answers. But was it a clanger, or expert trolling? Nobody knows exactly what solemn blood oaths Marvel uses to prevent spoilers.
body: Invited by Variety magazine to offer up a line from Doomsday “completely out of context”, Harbour thought for a moment, adopted the Russian accent of his Red Guardian character and came out with: “You … are Tony Stark.” Which is quite a thing to say about a film whose entire marketing campaign so far has depended on us accepting that Iron Man remains dead, and that the actor who used to play him, Robert Downey Jr, is playing Victor von Doom instead.

So what’s going on? The simplest and most likely explanation is that Harbour is trolling us, that Stark is not in the movie at all, and we’re all just fools. The new trailer for Doomsday, premiered last weekend at Disney’s D23 event in Anaheim, leans heavily into the prevailing wisdom that the film’s villain will be the tyrannical, unstoppable baddie of spurious eastern European extraction that Stan Lee and Jack Kirby dreamed up in 1962.

articles.title: ‘We’re barely above porn’: why would a film-maker choose to make a deliberately bad ‘mockbuster’?
articles.summary: With a tiny budget and six days, Anthony Frith directed a film for the studio behind Sharknado – and then made Mockbuster, a documentary about the experience. Directors don’t tend to appreciate having their films eviscerated by critics.
body: This is, however, exactly what I do to the Australian film-maker Anthony Frith. I’ve even prepared a zinger for the occasion. “Your film is a lemon that’s been eaten by a turkey then dumped into a vat of curdled mayonnaise,” I say.
Frith isn’t upset. He even smiles. “That’s a fair assessment,” he replies.

The production I’m sledging isn’t his well-directed, enjoyably staged and sometimes laugh-out-loud funny new documentary Mockbuster. It’s his other film, which Mockbuster charts the making-of: a pulpy, rinky-dink adaptation of The Land That Time Forgot, in which an Australian naval vessel is attacked by a Russian submarine, leaving the crew stranded on a dinosaur-populated island where they’re assaulted by unconvincing accents and various CGI beasts.
points: With a tiny budget and six days, Anthony Frith directed a film for the studio behind Sharknado – and then made Mockbuster, a documentary about the experience.

articles.title: Prince Harry and six others face privacy case legal bill of up to £34.5m
articles.summary: The seven claimants, who include Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, have to pay the Daily Mail publisher an initial £9.54m in the next seven days after losing a privacy case.
body: Prince Harry and six other public figures face paying up to £34.5m to the publisher of the Daily Mail after a High Court judge imposed an exceptional order for legal costs over their failed privacy case.
The seven claimants, also including Sir Elton John and Liz Hurley, must pay an initial £9.54m by Friday of next week to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL).

The judge ruled that the case was a rare one in which the claimants should have to pay far in excess of the costs that had been agreed before trial, criticising how they presented their claims as "unreasonable to a high degree".
On 7 July, Judge Mr Justice Nicklin dismissed the claims of unlawful information-gathering, which ANL denied.

articles.title: The Odyssey becomes highest grossing R-rated film of all time
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan’s epic has achieved $1.35bn at the global box office, overtaking 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine. The Odyssey has overtaken Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest grossing R-rated film of all time.
body: According to figures compiled by the Numbers, Christopher Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s epic poem has achieved $1.35bn (£990m) at the worldwide box office, compared with the Ryan Reynolds/Hugh Jackman superhero movie, which stands at $1.34bn (£980m) since its release in 2024.

A R-rating as designated by the Motion Picture Association requires anyone under 17 to be accompanied by an adult, and is normally seen as a brake on box office expectations. In its citation, the MPA said The Odyssey was given an R-rating “for violence and some language”.
In the UK, The Odyssey has been rated 15 for “strong violence”, while in Australia it has an M-rating for “mature themes, violence and coarse language”.

Other R-rated features to do well include Nolan’s previous film Oppenheimer, which benefited from the “Barbenheimer” craze to amass $983m worldwide, the Joaquin Phoenix-starring Joker ($1.1bn), and the two standalone Deadpool movies ($782m and $786m respectively).

articles.title: ‘Voice of Hind Rajab’ Director Slams Israeli Military Investigation Into 5-Year-Old Girl’s Death as a “Smokescreen”
articles.summary: "What is needed now is not a public relations operation. What is needed is justice (delivered by an independent authority) for Hind and for all the victims of the genocide in Gaza," Kaouther Ben Hania, who helmed the Oscar-nominated docudrama, said, dismissing the criminal probe announced this week…
body: The director of the Oscar-nominated docudrama The Voice of Hind Rajab has criticized the Israeli military investigation announced this week into the death of the 5-year-old Palestinian girl, who was killed after Israeli forces fired on her family’s car in Gaza City.
“This announcement is a smokescreen,” Kaouther Ben Hania said on Instagram, questioning why it took so long to launch the investigation.

She added, “Look at the cases the Israeli military is choosing to speak about today: they are precisely the ones that international public opinion has made impossible to ignore. And what about all the others? Those whose names we will never know because their deaths never broke through the wall of international indifference? Meanwhile, the Israeli military continues to kill Palestinians in Gaza, while the occupation intensifies in the West Bank.”

Suggesting that Israel’s move to launch a criminal investigation into Rajab’s death is a “public relations operation,” Ben Hania wrote, “What is needed is justice (delivered by an independent authority) for Hind and for all the victims of the genocide in Gaza.”

articles.title: Tupac murder accused told police in 2008 his nephew fired fatal shots
articles.summary: A recording of the interview Duane Davis conducted with detectives was played to the jury.
body: The man accused of orchestrating the murder of Tupac Shakur told police more than a decade later that he handed the gun used in the drive-by shooting to a passenger who then passed it to his nephew who opened fire on the rapper.

Duane "Keffe D" Davis is on trial in Las Vegas, charged with one count of murder with a deadly weapon over the killing of the rap superstar in 1996. On Thursday jurors heard a recording of a police interview with Davis in 2008.
Prosecutors allege that although Davis did not fire the gun that killed Shakur, he ordered the shooting and supplied the deadly weapon to further criminal conduct for the gang he helped lead.
His lawyer Michael Sanft has argued that what his client had previously said of his involvement cannot be believed.
